'''Álvaro Jaime Mones Sibillotte''' (born 7 August 1942 in [[Montevideo]]) is a Uruguayan [[biologist]] and [[Paleontology|paleontologist]].<ref>[http://www.mec.gub.uy/munhina/biograf11.htm Uruguayan biologists] {{in lang|es}}</ref>

The extinct ''[[Josephoartigasia monesi]]'' is named after him, for his study of [[South America|South American]] [[Rodent|rodents]],<ref name="Rinderknecht">{{cite journal | last1=Rinderknecht |first1=Andrés |last2=Blanco |first2=R. Ernesto |date=January 2008 |title=The largest fossil rodent |journal=Proceedings of the Royal Society B |volume=275 |issue=1637|pages=923–8 |doi=10.1098/rspb.2007.1645 |pmid=18198140 |pmc=2599941}}</ref> including its relative ''[[Josephoartigasia magna]]''.<ref name="Francis1966">{{cite journal |last1=Francis |first1=J. C. |last2=Mones |first2=A. |year=1966 |title=''Artigasia magna'' n. g., n. sp. (Eumegamyinae), un roedor gigantesco de la época Pliocena Superior de las Barrancas de San Gregorio, Departamento de San José, República Oriental del Uruguay |trans-title=''Artigasia magna'' n. g., n. sp. (Eumegamyinae), a giant rodent from the Upper Pliocene epoch from the St Gregorio Hills, Department of San José, Eastern Republic of Uruguay |url=https://www.academia.edu/17311374 |journal=Kraglieviana |language=Spanish |issue=3 |pages=89–100}}</ref>
